messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content:
In domestic cats and many wild felids—including lions—the **coat‑color gene** (the *MC1R* locus) follows classic Mendelian dominance: the allele that produces eumelanin (black/brown pigment) is dominant over the allele that produces pheomelanin (red/yellow pigment).  

So, if a lion carries one copy of the “black” allele and one copy of the “yellow” allele, the animal will display the darker, eumelanin‑based coloration. This is why most lions have a tawny or brownish coat rather than a bright yellow or orange one.

(If you’re curious about other traits—like mane development in male lions—that’s more a case of hormonal regulation than simple dominance at a single locus.)
